title: How salvation works

line.younger: The good news of Jesus in nine pictures: what went wrong between people and God, what God did about it, and the new life he gives.
line.older: The gospel in nine pictures: made for God, broken from him, and brought back by God's own act in Christ, a gift received by faith.

poster: A wide land split by a deep gap. On the left, people stand at the edge and look across. On the right the ground rises into light, and a thin gold line already reaches out from the light over the gap.

frames.name: Made for God
frames.still: One wide land with no break in it. A tree grows near the middle, people stand beside it, and a gold line runs from the light on the right down to the ground where the people stand, joining them to it.
frames.younger: God made people in his own image, to know him, to love him and to be happy with him for ever. In the beginning nothing stood between people and God.
frames.older: The story starts with a gift, not a problem. God made human beings in his own image, to know him and show what he is like, and to love him and be happy in him for ever (the family catechism, questions 7 and 8). Nothing stood between people and God.

verse.text: So God created man in His own image; in the image of God He created him; male and female He created them.

frames.name: We turned away
frames.still: The land has cracked in two. The left side, with the people on it, has slid away and down, and a deep, dark gap lies between it and the light. The gold line now stops short, in the air above God's side of the gap.
frames.younger: But people turned away from God and went their own way. The Bible calls that sin. Sin is when we do not love God and others the way we should, and everyone has done it. Sin breaks us and keeps us away from God.
frames.older: People turned from God to their own way, and every one of us has followed (Romans 3:23). Sin is more than a list of wrong things done. It is a break: with God, with each other, inside ourselves. Isaiah says our sins have “built barriers between you and your God” (Isaiah 59:2).

say.older: People turned from God to their own way, and every one of us has followed. Sin is more than a list of wrong things done. It is a break: with God, with each other, inside ourselves. Isaiah says our sins have “built barriers between you and your God”.

verse.text: for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God

frames.name: We cannot mend it
frames.still: On the left, the people have piled up blocks at the edge of the gap to reach across. The pile leans out over the gap and stops far short of the other side, and one block tumbles down into the dark.
frames.younger: People have always tried to fix it themselves: by being good enough, by trying harder, by doing more. It never reaches. The Bible says we are saved by God's gift, not by being good enough.
frames.older: Every age builds its towers: be good enough, try harder, earn your way back. The Bible says plainly that the gap is too wide. Salvation is “the gift of God, not by works, so that no one can boast” (Ephesians 2:8-9). That is hard news for anyone who likes to earn things, and good news for anyone who knows they cannot.

say.older: Every age builds its towers: be good enough, try harder, earn your way back. The Bible says plainly that the gap is too wide. Salvation is “the gift of God, not by works, so that no one can boast”. That is hard news for anyone who likes to earn things, and good news for anyone who knows they cannot.

verse.text: not by works, so that no one can boast.

frames.name: God comes to us
frames.still: From the light on the right, the gold line reaches all the way across the gap and comes down to the ground on the people's side. Where it lands, a new figure stands among the people: the Son, come to them.
frames.younger: So God came to us. God the Father loved the world so much that he sent his Son. Jesus, the Son of God, became a man and lived among us. God did not wait for us to climb back. He came all the way to our side.
frames.older: Then God crosses the gap from his own side. The Father sends the Son, not to win over an unwilling God, but because he already loves the world (John 3:16). The eternal Son becomes one of us, fully God and fully man: “The Word became flesh and made His dwelling among us” (John 1:14).

say.older: Then God crosses the gap from his own side. The Father sends the Son, not to win over an unwilling God, but because he already loves the world. The eternal Son becomes one of us, fully God and fully man: “The Word became flesh and made His dwelling among us”.

verse.text: For God so loved the world that He gave His one and only Son, that everyone who believes in Him shall not perish but have eternal life.

frames.name: The cross
frames.still: An empty cross stands on a small hill at the edge of the gap. The two sides of the land have come back together, and a gold seam runs down the place where the break was.
frames.younger: Jesus never did anything wrong, but he died on a cross for our sins. He took the punishment for our sin, so that the break between us and God could be mended. God's love did it: the Father sent the Son, and the Son gave himself.
frames.older: At the cross the break is mended, and God is the one who mends it. “Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures” (1 Corinthians 15:3), “the righteous for the unrighteous, to bring you to God” (1 Peter 3:18). The Father and the Son are not on opposite sides here: “God proves His love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us” (Romans 5:8).

say.older: At the cross the break is mended, and God is the one who mends it. “Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures”, “the righteous for the unrighteous, to bring you to God”. The Father and the Son are not on opposite sides here: “God proves His love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us”.

verse.text: For Christ also suffered for sins once for all, the righteous for the unrighteous, to bring you to God.

frames.name: The empty tomb
frames.still: Beside the cross, a tomb is cut into the rock. Its round stone is rolled away, and gold light shines from the open doorway.
frames.younger: Jesus was buried, but on the third day God raised him from the dead. He is alive. Death could not hold him, and the mending is real.
frames.older: He was buried, and on the third day he was raised, in his body, not as an idea (1 Corinthians 15:4). The resurrection is God's sign that the cross did what it set out to do: Jesus “was delivered over to death for our trespasses and was raised to life for our justification” (Romans 4:25).

say.older: He was buried, and on the third day he was raised, in his body, not as an idea. The resurrection is God's sign that the cross did what it set out to do: Jesus “was delivered over to death for our trespasses and was raised to life for our justification”.

verse.text: He was delivered over to death for our trespasses and was raised to life for our justification.

frames.name: Trusting him
frames.still: One person on the joined land stands with hands open and raised. The gold line comes all the way down to where they stand. They have not climbed anywhere: the light has come to them.
frames.younger: How is this gift received? By trusting Jesus and turning back to God. Faith is not one more job to earn it. It is like resting your whole weight on a chair you trust to hold you. Grace is God's love that you do not have to earn.
frames.older: The gift is received, not earned. Jesus said, “Repent and believe in the gospel” (Mark 1:15): turn around, and trust him. Faith is not a work that pays for anything. It is empty hands taking what is given: “it is by grace you have been saved through faith, and this not from yourselves; it is the gift of God” (Ephesians 2:8).

say.older: The gift is received, not earned. Jesus said, “Repent and believe in the gospel”: turn around, and trust him. Faith is not a work that pays for anything. It is empty hands taking what is given: “it is by grace you have been saved through faith, and this not from yourselves; it is the gift of God”.

verse.text: and the kingdom of God is near. Repent and believe in the gospel!

frames.name: New life
frames.still: The person now stands with others at the open door of a lit house, a small gold flame above them, and a young green tree grows on the land where the break was.
frames.younger: Everyone who trusts Jesus is forgiven and given a whole new life. God makes them his own child, gives them his Holy Spirit to live in them, and puts them in his family, the church, with all his people.
frames.older: God gives more than a clean record. Those who belong to Christ are forgiven, adopted as God's children (by the Spirit they cry, “Abba! Father!”, Romans 8:15), given the Holy Spirit, and joined to his people. As Paul puts it, “if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away” (2 Corinthians 5:17).

say.older: God gives more than a clean record. Those who belong to Christ are forgiven, adopted as God's children (by the Spirit they cry, “Abba! Father!”), given the Holy Spirit, and joined to his people. As Paul puts it, “if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away”.

verse.text: Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away. Behold, the new has come!

frames.name: The life to come
frames.still: The whole land is one again. On the right a city gate stands open with gold light pouring from it, a river runs out toward us, and people walk in along the road.
frames.younger: And this is only the start. One day God will make everything new. He will live with his people for ever, and there will be no more crying, no more pain and no more death.
frames.older: The story ends where it began, with God and his people together, and more than before. John hears that “the dwelling place of God is with man”, and that “He will wipe away every tear from their eyes” (Revelation 21:3-4). Christians differ on many details of the last things. On this hope they speak together.

say.older: The story ends where it began, with God and his people together, and more than before. On this hope they speak together.

verse.text: and there will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain, for the former things have passed away.

think.younger: God did not wait for people to climb back to him. He came all the way to them. What does that tell you about God? Talk about it with a parent, a pastor or a leader you trust.
think.older: Which is harder to believe: that you need this gift, or that it is free? Talk it over with a parent, a pastor or a leader you trust.

differ.text: All Christians confess that sinners are saved by God's grace, through Jesus' death and resurrection, and not by their own good deeds. Churches differ on the place of baptism, on how God's choosing and our choosing fit together, and on whether a believer can fall away. This moving picture does not choose between them. The different views are set out in

care: If this leaves you feeling too bad to be forgiven, or afraid, remember what Paul says: “While we were still sinners, Christ died for us” (Romans 5:8). Nobody has to carry that alone. Talk with a parent, a pastor or a leader you trust, or look at Find Help.

frames.text: God made people in his own image, to know him, to love him and to be happy with him for ever.
But people turned away from God and went their own way. The Bible calls that sin. Sin is when we do not love God and others the way we should, and everyone has done it.
So God came to us. God the Father loved the world so much that he sent his Son. Jesus, the Son of God, became a man and lived among us.
Jesus was buried, but on the third day God raised him from the dead. He is alive.
How is this gift received? By trusting Jesus and turning back to God. Faith is not one more job to earn it. Grace is God's love that you do not have to earn.
